Drone Wall Rises: Ukraine Bets on Its Best Corps — A two-week roundup of the Russia-Ukraine war: Ukraine's 1st and 3rd Corps take command of the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk defense, Russia launches a major ballistic missile strike on Kyiv, and Ukrainian forces hit a record 21 Russian oil refineries in August. Plus new weapons debuts, a Banderol missile strike on Pechenihy, and the latest on Russia's fuel and power shortages.

‘No Scenario That Would Require It’: Putin Denies New Russian Mobilization – Again — Putin has again denied that Russia is preparing a new mobilization, calling the reports an “information attack” aimed at disrupting upcoming State Duma elections. His repeated denials come amid growing speculation that Moscow is preparing to expand military recruitment.

Russia to Close Goethe-Institut Branches in Retaliation Against Germany — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Russia would close Goethe-Institut branches across the country in response to Germany’s measures following an explosives-laden drone incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

Russia Puts TV Propaganda Chiefs Under Guard Amid Threat of Ukrainian Strikes — Russia’s National Guard has stepped up security for senior television executives and prominent presenters, reportedly amid fears they could be targeted by Ukraine.

Tusk Calls Polish Drone Component Plant Fire Sabotage — Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a fire at a WB Electronics plant producing components for unmanned systems was deliberately damaged in an act of sabotage and accused Russia of using cryptocurrency to finance the operation. Authorities have not reached the same conclusion, including a separate blaze at an aviation-components facility in Lublin.

Ukraine’s Drones Reach Moscow’s Doorstep, Hit Homes and Sochi Port — Russian officials say Ukrainian drones hit residential buildings in Moscow Region and caused a fire at a factory, while a separate attack hit the Black Sea port of Sochi.

Ukraine to Help Europe Close Defense Gaps as Russia Threat Grows — Ukraine will join a new European initiative to identify and rapidly address defense gaps, drawing on its battlefield experience against Russia. The effort comes as Europe faces Russian hybrid threats and uncertainty over the future US military role in NATO.

Russian Drones Hit Kyiv Region, Injuring 1 Amid Damaged Warehouses and Buildings — Russian forces attacked Kyiv region on Thursday, Sept. 3, injuring one person and damaging warehouses, an administrative building, a store, and kiosks. Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia launched 163 drones overnight, with 135 shot down or suppressed.

EU Summons Russia Envoys, Eyes Sanctions After Germany Drone ‘Attack’ — EU ministers agreed to advance sanctions against 1,600 Russia-linked individuals and entities after an explosive-laden drone incident at Leipzig airport. They also backed tougher Russian visa restrictions and discussed additional air-defense aid for Ukraine.

Leipzig Case Revives Push for EU Russian Visa Ban — A suspected sabotage plot at Leipzig airport is intensifying EU calls for tougher restrictions on Russian travelers. Ministers also debated the future of the EU’s foreign policy service and negotiations over the bloc’s next long-term budget.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 2, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 2, 2026.

Germany’s Response to Attempted Russian Drone Attack at Leipzig Airport Criticized as Too Weak — Germany attributed the Leipzig/Halle sabotage plot to Russia but kept describing it as a hybrid attack, prompting criticism from Baltic and security officials.

Russian Strike Hits Multi-Story Residential Building in Odesa, Injuring 17, Including 3 Children — A Russian overnight air attack damaged a 21-story residential building in Odesa, injuring 17 people, including 3 children. Apartments on eight floors and several cars were damaged, while emergency and municipal crews continue clearing the aftermath.

Foreign Airlines Begin Suspending Flights to Russia Following Kyiv’s Warning That Its Airspace Is Unsafe — Airlines began canceling flights to Russia after Kyiv warned that expanding drone operations were making the country’s airspace increasingly unsafe for civilian aviation.

Zelensky Says Ukraine, Germany Finalizing Drone Deal as Kyiv Expands Defense Network — Ukraine and Germany are finalizing a bilateral Drone Deal covering joint production and defense cooperation, building on several projects already underway.

Norway Seizes Russian Ship to Enforce $4.2B Naftogaz Award — Norwegian authorities seized a Russian vessel in the Arctic at Naftogaz’s request as the Ukrainian energy company seeks compensation for assets illegally seized by Russia following its 2014 annexation of Crimea.

Russia Strikes Ukraine's Largest Wine Retailer, Alcohol Importer — Russian forces destroyed the central logistics warehouse belonging to Okwine and Wine Hunters, Ukraine's largest wine retailer and alcohol importer. The companies were actively restocking their inventory following a previous missile strike in July when this second attack occurred.

Rubio Says CIA Chief Visited Moscow Just to Keep Intel Ties Open — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday, Sept. 2, that CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s recent Moscow visit was intended to maintain communication between American and Russian intelligence services. His comments followed previous speculations that Ratcliffe’s meetings centered on Russia’s war against Ukraine or Moscow’s possible actions toward NATO.

21 Banks Used in Halushchenko’s Bail Payments, 4 of Them State Owned — According to Ukrainian authorities, about 85 accounts were used across 21 banks – four of them state-owned – to post Hr.150 million (roughly $3.3 million) in bail for former Energy Minister Herman Halushchenko. The transfers are central to the new anti-graft probe dubbed “Forrest Gump,” which is investigating the suspected money-laundering scheme.

Zelensky Demands Accountability Following ‘Absolutely Disgraceful’ SBU-HUR Shootout in Kyiv — President Volodymyr Zelensky called the Wednesday, Sept. 2 shootout between personnel from the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) and Ukraine’s Military Intelligence (HUR) “absolutely disgraceful” and demanded accountability. He said the Prosecutor General’s Office and the State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) would establish the facts and review the conduct of everyone involved.

EU Postpones Extension of Russia Sanctions Until Sept. 9 — According to European Pravda on Wednesday, Sept. 2, EU ambassadors postponed a decision on renewing sanctions against more than 3,000 Russian individuals and companies until Sept. 9. The restrictions, imposed on Russia over its war against Ukraine, are due to expire on Sept. 15, while Slovakia reportedly opposed a one-year extension.

2 Suspects Linked to Leipzig Airport Hybrid Attack, EU to Retaliate — According to Reuters on Wednesday, Sept. 2, the EU said it would step up pressure on Russia after two Russia-linked suspects were identified in connection with an attempted drone attack at Leipzig Halle Airport in Germany. Germany blamed Moscow, while Russia denied involvement and summoned Germany’s charge d’affaires, further straining bilateral relations.

Maldives Used as Route for Russian Sanctions Evasion — The Maldives has reportedly become a transit route for hundreds of millions of dollars in restricted Western goods headed to Russia. According to The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday, Sept. 1, cargo is transferred through Malé airport and flown to Moscow, highlighting another channel used to bypass sanctions imposed on the country in response to the war against Ukraine.

Ukraine to Introduce Yellow and Red Air Alert Levels — Ukraine will introduce yellow and red air alert levels as part of an overhaul of its national warning system. Yellow alerts will generally signal drone raids, while red alerts will cover missile threats, including ballistic and large-scale attacks. Officials will review the criteria weekly as Russia continues using drones to disrupt civilian life and economic activity.

Ukraine’s New Defense Minister Tells Europe: $27B Needed Urgently — Ukraine’s new defense minister Khmara urged Europe to provide $27 billion, chiefly for air defenses, ahead of expected winter attacks. EU officials agreed but made no immediate commitments. Meanwhile, Germany accused Russia of terrorism.

Russian Strike on Dnipro Kills 2, Injures 8, Damages Homes and Schools — Russia attacked Dnipro overnight, killing 2 people and injuring 8, including 3 who were hospitalized in critical condition. The strike damaged apartment buildings and educational institutions, hit food warehouses and sparked fires that emergency crews later extinguished.

Ukraine Seeks Billions From EU for Patriot Missiles — Ukraine has requested several billion euros from the EU’s €90 billion support loan to buy PAC-3 Patriot air defense missiles. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said member states are reviewing the request and expressed confidence about its progress. Since June, the EU has disbursed €8.5 billion from the loan for Ukrainian drones and missiles.

Germany to Send New Air Defense Packages to Ukraine as Russia Escalates Drone Attacks — Germany will send Ukraine new air defense packages in September as Russia intensifies its drone campaign, with around 1,500 drones launched in just four days at the end of August. The two countries are also finalizing a new drone cooperation deal.

Donbas: The Ukrainian Roots That Survived — In this second part of a 2-part series, Kate Turska turns to what Russia's mythology can't explain: Ukrainian poets, soldiers and civil resistance rooted in the very region Moscow claimed as its own. From Azov's leadership to the Yellow Ribbon movement under occupation, and Russia's ongoing efforts to indoctrinate children today, Turska argues that identity manufactured by an enemy can still fail to take hold.

Germany Probes Two Sabotage Attacks on Power Grid — Germany is investigating two attacks on power substations as authorities warn of a growing threat of sabotage and hybrid attacks targeting critical infrastructure. The incidents came as Berlin formally blamed Russia for an attempted drone attack at a strategic airport.

Russia Fines Google, Telegram, Pinterest Over Non-Compliant Content — Moscow’s Tagansky court on Wednesday fined Google $87,054 for not removing a chauffeur app, Telegram $43,529 for not removing non-state complaint war messages, and Pinterest $123,715 for not taking down LGBT-related content. The fines follow numerous precedents, with the Kremlin fining Western tech firms for failing to comply with its draconian information laws.

Zelensky Names Sviatoslav Zaits Ground Forces Chief — President Volodymyr Zelensky dismissed Maj. Gen. Hennadiy Shapovalov as commander of Ukraine’s Ground Forces and appointed Brig. Gen. Sviatoslav Zaits to replace him. Zaits previously commanded the 20th Army Corps and served in the Air Assault Forces. The two presidential decrees did not state a reason for the leadership change.

Pegasus Turns Russia-Bound Jets Back After Zelensky Warning — Passengers reported waiting more than 10 hours after Pegasus halted several Russia-bound services, citing the “airspace situation.” Two aircraft already over Europe returned to Turkey, while dozens of departures were listed as canceled following overnight drone attacks and temporary restrictions at Moscow’s Vnukovo airport.

Kyiv Shootout Between SBU and HUR – What We Know — Servicemen from HUR reportedly fired at the SBU in Kyiv on Wednesday when the latter was working to foil an operation by Russia’s FSB. The case reportedly involves the deputy commander of the Russian Volunteer Corps (RDK), with the State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) intervening at the scene.

Drone Incident in Leipzig: the Trail Leads to Russia — Germany has blamed Russia for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport and announced new sanctions. European media urge stronger action against Russia’s hybrid warfare, while warning against escalation. Commentators call for increased defence and support for Ukraine, noting that sabotage, disinformation and other low-level attacks may form part of a broader Russian campaign against Europe.

Ukraine Denies Putin’s Claim of Capturing Kozacha Lopan Near Russian Border — Ukraine says Kozacha Lopan, 7 kilometers from Russia, remains under Ukrainian control despite Moscow’s claim of its capture. Fighting continues around the village, where Ukrainian forces say Russia has suffered 178 soldiers killed and 210 wounded.
CARTOON: Bizarre Bazaar at Bishkek Summit — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

Medvedev Threatens ‘Direct Strike’ on German Military Factories, Hints at Attacks on Berlin — Russia’s former president also threatened Western leaders traveling to Kyiv by train, escalating Moscow’s rhetoric after Germany accused Russia of a drone attack on Leipzig Airport.

Machine-Gun Pickup Escorts Putin Convoy in Vladivostok — Videos shared by Russian Telegram channels show a heavily guarded presidential motorcade traveling from Vladivostok airport, with a pickup apparently carrying an anti-aircraft machine gun. Troops and military vehicles were positioned along the route, while residents reported major traffic disruption as Putin arrived on Wednesday for the Eastern Economic Forum.

Moscow Mayor Says 8,670 Drones Tried to Hit Capital in August — Moscow’s mayor claimed that Ukraine launched 8,670 drones against the Russian capital and the surrounding region in August, with 795 shot down en route to Moscow. The staggering number, if accurate, is on par with the total number of Russian drones launched across the entirety of Ukraine in July 2026.

Russia Secretly Helps Iran Develop Supersonic Cruise Missiles, FT Reports — Russia has secretly assisted Iran in developing supersonic cruise missile technology under a covert program codenamed C430L, according to a Financial Times investigation based on leaked correspondence, travel records, and Russian military patents.

Ukrainian War Documentary ‘Brace For Oblivion’ Wins in Ireland, Comes to Kyiv — Filmed over nearly four years on Ukraine’s front lines, Xackery Irving’s documentary “Brace For Oblivion” follows seven civilians who became soldiers after Russia’s full-scale invasion. After winning an international award in Galway, the film returns to Ukraine for a special screening in Kyiv.

Russian Drone Tears Into Central Kyiv Apartment Building, University Also Hit — A Russian drone struck a residential building in central Kyiv, injuring seven people, as the capital came under another daytime attack on Wednesday. Multiple explosions were reported across the city, with fires and damage reported in Kyiv and the surrounding region.

Fire Erupts at Russian Rocket Engine Plant in Perm — A fire broke out at Proton-PM, a major Russian rocket engine manufacturer in Perm. The plant produces engines for Proton and Angara rockets and is part of the state-run Roscosmos space corporation. No casualties were reported.

Kyiv, Odesa Hit in Massive Russian Attack as 10 People Are Wounded — Russia launched 174 drones and 4 missiles at Ukraine overnight, primarily targeting Kyiv and Odesa. At least 10 people were wounded, including a child, while residential buildings, warehouses, schools and other civilian infrastructure were damaged.

Ukraine Foils Alleged FSB Terror Plot Against Russian Opposition Leader — Ukraine’s SBU and HUR say they prevented an FSB-planned attack against a Russian opposition leader visiting Ukraine. The development comes as the Russian Volunteer Corps says it has lost contact with deputy commander Kaplunov, whose disappearance remains officially unconfirmed.

Drone-Led Ukrainian Offensive Retakes Ground in Critical Eastern Front Sector — Ukraine’s 3rd Army Corps is leading a methodical counteroffensive north and east of Lyman, making significant gains, cutting Russian supply routes and threatening to encircle hundreds of Russian troops in a growing salient, amid heavy drone strikes.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 1, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 1, 2026.

Putin Claims Ukraine Will ‘Crumble,’ Threatens Massive Energy Strikes and Rules Out Talks With ‘Terrorists’ — Putin used his Bishkek press conference to claim accelerating Russian gains, threaten new attacks on Ukraine’s energy system and lash out at Zelensky and Germany, while acknowledging Ukrainian strikes are damaging Russian refineries.

Putin Praises Iran’s ‘Courage and Resilience’ Amid War With US, Pledges Support — Putin praised Iran’s resistance amid its ongoing war with the US and said Moscow was providing Tehran with “necessary assistance” and supplies as the two deepen their strategic partnership.

Germany Concludes Russia Behind Attempted Drone Attack, Announces Retaliation — After weeks of holding back from publicly naming Moscow, Germany formally held Russia responsible for the explosive-laden drone found at Leipzig/Halle Airport and announced diplomatic and sanctions measures.

Zelensky Warns International Airlines: ‘Safe Days in Russia’s Skies Are Over’ — Zelensky said Russian airspace is becoming increasingly unsafe as Ukraine steps up strikes on military and war-supporting targets, while still pausing operations when partners request diplomatic windows.

Russia Launches Massive Air Attack on Odesa, Homes and Infrastructure Damaged — Russian forces launched another large-scale attack on Odesa overnight, damaging residential buildings and infrastructure as multiple types of aerial weapons targeted the city.

US Treasury Secretary Says Russia’s G20 Presence Did Not Disrupt Talks Despite EU Anger — US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended engaging Moscow at the G20 despite European objections to Russia’s return while its war against Ukraine continues.

Lawmakers Kill Parcel Tax Reform, Block Audit Chamber Vote Hours After PM Warns of $27B Defense Gap — Ukraine's parliament has rejected eight bills that would have taxed low-value imported parcels, and failed to approve a vote on selecting six new accounting chamber members – both conditions of EU and IMF financing – hours after Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi urged lawmakers to clear bills tied to $30 billion in expected 2026 support.

Hungary Blocks Ukraine’s EU Clusters For Third Time, Offers to Unblock Them in Exchange for Minority Rights Progress — Hungary blocked Ukraine’s second and third EU accession clusters for a third time on Tuesday, Sept.1, though Budapest said it would lift its objection if Kyiv shows progress on protecting the rights of Ukraine’s Hungarian minority. The refusal again prevented the EU from approving screening results needed to advance negotiations because unanimity from all 27 EU member states is

Vivat Loses 35,500 Books to Russian Strike, Damage Tops $370,000 — A Russian strike on a warehouse in Sviatopetrivske, Kyiv region, destroyed more than 35,500 books belonging to publisher Vivat, worth over Hr 16.6 million ($372,800), the company told Kyiv Post. Vivat is also tallying losses from strikes on partner distributors and said some shipments remain paused as a result.

Ababahalamaha Finds New Warehouse, Plans to Resume Shipping Next Week — Ukrainian children's book publisher Ababahalamaha, whose warehouse was destroyed in a recent Russian strike, wrote on Facebook that it has secured a new warehouse and is loading it with books. The company expects to resume shipping orders as early as next week and thanked customers for their continued support during the disruption.

Ukraine Warns Airlines Against Traveling Through Russian Airspace — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned airlines, insurers and airport operators on Tuesday, Sept. 1, against traveling through Russian airspace as it becomes increasingly dangerous due to drone activity linked to Moscow’s war. Zelensky said civilian carriers should reconsider flying to Moscow, St. Petersburg and other major Russian destinations.

US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll Resigns Amid Tensions With Hegseth — US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has resigned after months of friction with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the White House confirmed Monday, Aug. 31. During his tenure, he helped the Trump administration lead contacts with Ukrainian and Russian officials aimed at advancing peace talks.

5 Wounded in Russian Strikes on Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian forces attacked five districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 50 times on Tuesday, Sept. 1, injuring five people. The strikes damaged civilian sites in the Dnipro, Nikopol, Kryvyi Rih and Synelnykove districts, sparking multiple fires.

Fedorov Says Palantir CEO Will Back Ukraine Defense Tech Company — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said Tuesday, Sept. 1, that he held meetings in Washington with US investors and venture funds to seek support for a new defense technology investment fund. Palantir CEO, Alex Karp, will become the first key investor, Fedorov says.

Koretskyi Hints at Austerity Measures to Relieve $27B Budget Shortfall — With a $27 billion defense budget deficit, Ukraine’s PM has warned of austerity measures and the redirection of Hr.70 billion (around $1.6 billion) to help fill the gap, while calling on lawmakers to adopt reform-related decisions needed to unlock foreign funding. The government is also eyeing the premature release of part of the EU’s €90 billion aid package to help plug the shortfall.

Ukraine’s Ombudsman Warns of ‘Systemic’ Mobilization Corruption, Says Men Can Be Smuggled Out for $70,000 — Ukrainian Parliamentary Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets has warned that corruption surrounding mobilization has become widespread, alleging that men can pay $10,000 to leave a military recruitment center, $15,000 to be released from its premises, or $50,000-$70,000 to be taken directly from a recruitment van and smuggled across the border.

Kremlin Hits 3 of Kyiv’s Biggest Retailers: Dnipro-M, VARUS, Aurora — Russian attacks damaged or destroyed distribution facilities belonging to Dnipro-M, VARUS, and Aurora in Kyiv and the Kyiv region between Aug. 29 and Aug. 31, the companies wrote. No casualties, not even minor injuries were reported. Dnipro-M and VARUS warned of delivery delays, while Aurora, hit for the third time in nine days, has not yet disclosed the scale of damage from its latest attack.

Former Defense Minister Fedorov Receives Military Deferment Via NGO — Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine’s former defense minister, received a deferment from mobilization via work with an NGO – but some lawmakers cast doubt on its legitimacy as the government hinted at upcoming plans to mobilize 30,000 troops per month to fend off a rumored 400,000-strong mobilization drive from Moscow.

11 EU States Push to End Foreign Policy Vetoes — Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Romania, Spain and Sweden have called for reforms to EU foreign policy decision-making, including exploring a shift from unanimity to qualified majority voting.

Xi Says China Ready to Step Up Peace Efforts in Ukraine, Middle East, Afghanistan — Xi Jinping said China is ready to strengthen communication with all parties and promote political settlements in Ukraine, the Middle East, and Afghanistan. At the SCO summit, he also called for stronger multilateral cooperation, security coordination, and a multipolar world.

Kallas Urges Countries to Give Ukraine Expiring Air Defense Missiles — EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called on countries to transfer soon-to-expire air defense interceptors to Ukraine, which is facing a shortage amid intensified Russian attacks. Speaking ahead of an informal meeting of EU defense ministers on Tuesday, Sept. 1, Kallas said July and August were the deadliest months for Ukrainian civilians.

Russia’s Starlink Rival Suffers Major Satellite Launch Failure — Russia’s second batch of 16 Rassvet satellites failed to reach its intended operational altitude, creating setback in Moscow’s effort to develop an alternative to Starlink, the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) reported. Some satellites are already losing altitude, with at least two reportedly heading toward reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. ISW said Russia lacks the launch capacity needed to rapidly establish stable, around-the-

Germany to Blame Russia For Airport Drone Incident: Reports — - Berlin is reportedly preparing to formally accuse a Russian intelligence agency of deploying an explosive-laden drone near Leipzig Airport, marking a potential escalation in Germany’s response to Moscow’s alleged hybrid attacks.

What Changed in Russia’s Drone War in Ukraine? — As Russia changed from occasional massive drone swarms to non-stop drone waves across Ukraine, Kyiv Post looked at the known numbers launched in recent days – which increased slightly compared to July while having a far larger share of jet-powered drones that complicate interceptions.

Graham’s ‘Sanctions Bill From Hell’ Against Russia Hits House Roadblock — Graham’s “sanctions bill from hell” passed the Senate 86-11 but is now facing a major roadblock in the House. The bill would let Trump impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying Russian energy, but both Democrats and some Republicans are pushing back.

Sporting Diplomacy in Odesa: Ukrainian Servicemen Take on Italian Pacifists — What happens when a group of Italian pacifists comes to a battered Ukrainian city to play soccer against Ukrainian soldiers in a tournament of the “beautiful game”? An encounter worthy of many toasts – with both Ukrainian and Italian wine.

Budanov Predicts Russian Drone Attacks Will Last Until State Duma Elections — Kyrylo Budanov said Russia is likely to continue mass drone attacks on Ukraine at least until its State Duma elections in September, as Moscow seeks to show voters a "picture of victory" despite lacking battlefield gains. In a comment to journalist Halyna Ostapovets, Budanov said Russia is resorting to terror because it "does not know how to do otherwise."

Russia Reportedly Strikes Odesa With KAB Guided Bombs for First Time — Russia reportedly struck Odesa with a KAB guided aerial bomb for the first time, in a major escalation of its attacks on the southern port city. The overnight assault also involved Shahed drones and Banderol munitions, causing power outages and fires.

Ukraine’s War Chest Shrinks as Europe Mulls Gamble with Russia Billions — Ukraine faces a €23.1 billion defense funding gap, prompting European allies to revisit the use of €210 billion in frozen Russian assets. But Belgium’s concerns over legal and financial liability remain the key obstacle to unlocking the money.

Ukraine Hits Russia’s Biggest Baltic Port as 516 Drones Reportedly Swarm Russian Skies — Ukraine launched a massive drone attack on Russia’s Leningrad Region, striking the Ust-Luga port and causing a fire. Russia claimed 516 drones were destroyed nationwide, while Estonia scrambled NATO fighter jets after several drones reportedly violated its airspace.

‘Russia Always Calculates Its Strikes to Destroy Lives’: Zelensky Says After Deadly Overnight Attack — President Volodymyr Zelensky said 12 people, including an Indian citizen, were killed and dozens injured in Russia’s overnight missile and drone attack on Ukraine. He said the strikes damaged residential and civilian infrastructure in Kyiv, the Kyiv region, Odesa, and several other regions.

Russia’s Overnight Attack Hits Romania Border Crossing, Targets Rescuers in Zaporizhzhia — Russia launched a combined overnight attack involving 218 Shahed drones and multiple missiles, mainly targeting Odesa and Kyiv regions. The attacks damaged the Orlivka crossing with Romania and targeted rescuers in Zaporizhzhia, while Ukraine reported neutralizing 199 aerial targets.

EU Frets over Kyiv’s Defences, ‘Hybrid’ Threat From Moscow — EU defense and foreign ministers will discuss strengthening Ukraine’s air defenses, new sanctions and using frozen Russian assets. They are also expected to address growing Russian hybrid attacks and sabotage across Europe.

India-Russia: A Changing Equation — India-Russia relations are being reshaped by record Russian oil exports to India, growing Indian fuel shipments to Russia, persistent trade imbalances, and efforts to develop alternative transport corridors. The partnership remains resilient, but faces pressures from sanctions, Ukraine, and India’s economic priorities.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 30, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on August 30, 2026.

Putin Sends Support to Jailed Ex-President as Armenia Drifts From Moscow — Putin sent birthday wishes to jailed former Armenian President Robert Kocharyan ahead of a meeting with Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, who holds more power than the largely ceremonial president, as Russia continues to lose its grip on Armenia.

Russia’s SCO Show Masks Shrinking Power, US Analyst Goble Says — As Putin met Xi Jinping and other leaders at the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, analyst Paul Goble told Kyiv Post that Russia is losing allies, soft power and influence, increasingly relying on other isolated states.

Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Russia’s Key Baltic Oil Port of Ust-Luga — A drone attack sparked a fire at Russia’s Ust-Luga port in Leningrad region, according to Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko. The Baltic facility is a major outlet for Russian oil exports.

European Ministers Boycott Russian Counterpart After Surprise US G20 Invitation — European officials refused to pose with Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov after Washington invited him to a G20 finance meeting in Asheville, triggering backlash over Russia’s diplomatic return.

Massive Russian Missile, Drone Attack on Kyiv and Region Kills 12, Injures Over 20 — Russia launched a large-scale missile and drone attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, killing 12 people and injuring over 20 others, including children.

Poland Opens Terrorism Probe Into Fire at Drone Factory — Polish prosecutors opened a terrorism investigation after a WB Electronics drone factory, which supplies both Kyiv and Warsaw militaries, caught fire early Monday, Aug. 31. Authorities said the blaze was deliberate and are investigating whether a foreign intelligence service was involved, though no suspects have been publicly identified.
